Microsoft Defender Engine (MsMpEng) spawning interactive shell - RoguePlanet CVE-2026-50656 AIInstallation High
Detects Microsoft Defender Malware Protection Engine processes (MsMpEng.exe, MpCmdRun.exe, NisSrv.exe) spawning cmd.exe / powershell.exe / pwsh.exe child processes. This is the direct post-exploitation behaviour of the RoguePlanet race-condition LPE which yields a SYSTEM-context command prompt parented to the Defender engine. Genuine Defender engine processes effectively never spawn interactive shells. Rationale: Article states the exploit 'spawn[s] command prompts with SYSTEM privileges via a Microsoft Defender race condition' - the only realistic parent for a race-won child in the Malware Protection Engine context is MsMpEng.exe (the Antimalware Service Executable that hosts the engine) or its siblings MpCmdRun.exe / NisSrv.exe. These engine processes do not normally spawn interactive shells, so the parent-child pair is high-fidelity. No external corroboration performed - article is dated 2026-06-17 and CVE-2026-50656 has no second-source coverage yet.
ATT&CKT1068 T1211
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Defender platform updates where MpCmdRun.exe legitimately spawns conhost.exe during signature refresh
  • Security engineers running 'mpcmdrun.exe -Scan' from an elevated shell that fork-chains a conhost child
  • Endpoint vendor compatibility testing tools that wrap Defender CLI calls
  • Defender Application Guard container launches creating conhost.exe under MsMpEngCP.exe
  • Microsoft-signed sample-submission helper that briefly spawns cmd.exe to invoke curl
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "MpCmdRun.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-SignatureUpdate","-Scan","-RemoveDefinitions","-RestoreDefaults","-RemoveSources","-EnableIntegrityServices"))
| where not (FileName =~ "conhost.exe" and InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "MpCmdRun.exe" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "services.exe")
Response runbook
1. Triage: Confirm InitiatingProcessSHA256 matches the legitimate signed Microsoft binary for MsMpEng / MpCmdRun (rules out parent-spoofing). Pull the child ProcessCommandLine and ProcessIntegrityLevel - true RoguePlanet exploitation will show SYSTEM integrity with no benign cmdline (no -Scan / -SignatureUpdate / -RemoveDefinitions arguments). 2. Contain: Isolate the host via Defender Live Response. Do NOT reboot - capture a memory image first (lsass + MsMpEng PIDs) because the race condition often leaves an injected/orphaned SYSTEM shell that's evidentially useful. Block outbound from the host. 3. Hunt: Pivot on (a) the AccountName that owned the user-mode prerequisite process in the prior 5 minutes, (b) DNS lookups to projectnightcrawler.dev from the host in the past 30 days (UC2), (c) any new local admin / scheduled task / service created post-spawn, (d) other endpoints where MsMpEng/MpCmdRun ever spawned cmd/ps in 90d.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","NisSrv.exe","MsMpEngCP.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","conhost.exe")
| where ProcessIntegrityLevel =~ "System" or AccountName =~ "system"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          ProcessIntegrityLevel, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any (@"\MsMpEng.exe", @"\MpCmdRun.exe", @"\NisSrv.exe", @"\MsMpEngCP.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any (@"\cmd.exe", @"\powershell.exe", @"\pwsh.exe", @"\conhost.exe")
| where SubjectUserSid =~ "S-1-5-18" or TargetUserSid =~ "S-1-5-18" or TokenElevationType has "1936"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType, SubjectUserSid
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Microsoft Defender Engine Spawning Interactive Shell (RoguePlanet CVE-2026-50656)
id: a8f3e5b2-1d4c-4e8f-9a2b-7c6f3d1e9b4a
description: Detects MsMpEng.exe / MpCmdRun.exe / NisSrv.exe spawning a command shell. This is the post-exploitation outcome of the RoguePlanet race-condition LPE in the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/microsoft/microsoft-working-on-defender-patch-for-rogueplanet-zero-day/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1211
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\MsMpEng.exe'
      - '\MpCmdRun.exe'
      - '\NisSrv.exe'
      - '\MsMpEngCP.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\conhost.exe'

  - Rare Defender platform-update helpers (verify with signed MpCmdRun command lines)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\MsMpEng.exe OR *\msmpeng.exe OR *\MSMPENG.EXE OR *\MpCmdRun.exe OR *\mpcmdrun.exe OR *\NisSrv.exe OR *\nissrv.exe) @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\conhost.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(MsMpEng|MpCmdRun|NisSrv|MsMpEngCP)\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|conhost)\.exe$/i
| IntegrityLevel=/system/i OR UserSid="S-1-5-18"
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Endpoint DNS / web access to Nightmare Eclipse exploit-hosting domain projectnightcrawler.dev AIWeaponization Medium
Detects DNS resolution or HTTP/S traffic to projectnightcrawler.dev, the self-hosted Git repository where researcher 'Nightmare Eclipse' publishes zero-day PoCs (RoguePlanet, BlueHammer, RedSun, GreenPlasma, MiniPlasma, YellowKey, UnDefend) after Microsoft removed their public GitHub/GitLab repos. Endpoint resolution of this domain outside of sanctioned threat-research workflows indicates an analyst, red team operator, or - more concerning - a regular user acquiring weaponisable exploit code. Rationale: projectnightcrawler.dev appears in the pre-extracted IOCs as the researcher's self-hosted git domain referenced by the article ('shared a proof-of-concept exploit in a self-hosted Git repository... Microsoft had previously targeted and removed their repos hosting exploits on GitHub and GitLab'). Because it's a single-purpose exploit-hosting domain, any endpoint resolution is high-signal-to-noise. No web corroboration performed - article is dated 2026-06-17 and the domain has no Sigma / abuse.ch / OTX presence yet.
ATT&CKT1588.005 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel and red-team analysts visiting the researcher's repo to study disclosed PoCs
  • Security engineers triaging this very bleepingcomputer article (the URL is embedded in the article body)
  • URL-defanging sandboxes (urlscan.io, any.run) detonating the article as a sample
  • Browser preview/prefetch fetching the link from a shared SOC chat
  • DNS recursive resolvers warming cache from a non-malicious lookup on the perimeter
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName startswith "sec-" or DeviceName startswith "redteam-" or DeviceName startswith "ir-" or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("urlscan-agent.exe","anyrun-agent.exe"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: Identify the InitiatingProcessFileName / ContextImageFileName that issued the lookup. Browser = likely curious analyst; git.exe / curl.exe / wget.exe / powershell.exe Invoke-WebRequest = direct PoC acquisition (much higher concern). Cross-reference DeviceId against your security/redteam asset list. 2. Contain: For non-security hosts, quarantine any executable / archive / .py / .ps1 files written to disk by the resolving process in the +/- 5 min window via Defender file search. Reset the user's session and consider a password rotation if the host showed evidence of PoC download. 3. Hunt: Run UC1 (Defender engine spawning shell) on the same DeviceId in the next 24-72 hours to confirm whether the acquired PoC was actually executed. Pivot on other Nightmare Eclipse-disclosed CVE IDs (BlueHammer, RedSun, UnDefend) - the same researcher's domain likely hosts those too, so the same network IOC covers multiple potential exploit chains.
union
(
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has "projectnightcrawler.dev"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Source="NetworkEvent"
),
(
    DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
    | where AdditionalFields has "projectnightcrawler.dev"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              RemoteUrl=tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).query),
              RemoteIP="", RemotePort=int(0), Source="DnsQuery"
)
| order by Timestamp desc
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has "projectnightcrawler.dev"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, EventResult
| union (
    ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has "projectnightcrawler.dev" or HttpHostName has "projectnightcrawler.dev"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery=HttpHostName, DnsResponseName=Url, EventResult
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: DNS Query to Nightmare Eclipse Exploit Hosting Domain (projectnightcrawler.dev)
id: c7d2e4f8-3b5a-4d9e-8f1c-2a5b7d3e6f8c
description: Detects endpoint DNS resolution of projectnightcrawler.dev, the self-hosted git domain used by researcher 'Nightmare Eclipse' to publish Windows zero-day PoCs (RoguePlanet, BlueHammer, RedSun, GreenPlasma, MiniPlasma, YellowKey, UnDefend) after Microsoft removed their GitHub/GitLab repos.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/microsoft/microsoft-working-on-defender-patch-for-rogueplanet-zero-day/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.t1588.005
  - attack.resource_development
logsource:
  category: dns
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|contains: 'projectnightcrawler.dev'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Sanctioned threat-research and red-team workstations
  - Security analysts triaging this advisory itself
level: medium
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:22 @QueryName:*projectnightcrawler.dev*) OR (source:windows.defender @RemoteUrl:*projectnightcrawler.dev*) OR (source:cloudtrail @requestParameters.queryName:*projectnightcrawler.dev*)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/projectnightcrawler\.dev/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, FirstIP4Record], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime FROM datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS WHERE (DNS.query="projectnightcrawler.dev" OR DNS.query="*.projectnightcrawler.dev") BY DNS.src DNS.query DNS.answer DNS.record_type | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-50656", "CVE-2026-33825", "CVE-2026-45498", "CVE-2026-45585", "CVE-2026-45586", "CVE-2020-17103")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-50656", "CVE-2026-33825", "CVE-2026-45498", "CVE-2026-45585", "CVE-2026-45586", "CVE-2020-17103")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.

ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-35273")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-35273")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35", "f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309") or SHA1 in~ ("2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35", "f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309") or MD5 in~ ("2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35", "f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309")

// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35", "f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"

union

        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("d317371cf2b4cd524849551ffd3b97d91edbc17f6b39c8693217383ba6a0370d", "9469268c421b7821f897deb2d4d2316b21ff5da35bef417aa4e284010ef78302", "3d8afae76c5982458849d21221e089ee161266a4248b12ea3048d1e79b76707e", "2ed6fdfa5f9120306167ba5d8d48a62dbe5fd0d05e87c33c9784f08698f8a66b", "3b48a334dcf0a08bed2a9766fd553474ae3014db600b65573dfee0f183e9d1d9") or SHA1 in~ ("d317371cf2b4cd524849551ffd3b97d91edbc17f6b39c8693217383ba6a0370d", "9469268c421b7821f897deb2d4d2316b21ff5da35bef417aa4e284010ef78302", "3d8afae76c5982458849d21221e089ee161266a4248b12ea3048d1e79b76707e", "2ed6fdfa5f9120306167ba5d8d48a62dbe5fd0d05e87c33c9784f08698f8a66b", "3b48a334dcf0a08bed2a9766fd553474ae3014db600b65573dfee0f183e9d1d9") or MD5 in~ ("d317371cf2b4cd524849551ffd3b97d91edbc17f6b39c8693217383ba6a0370d", "9469268c421b7821f897deb2d4d2316b21ff5da35bef417aa4e284010ef78302", "3d8afae76c5982458849d21221e089ee161266a4248b12ea3048d1e79b76707e", "2ed6fdfa5f9120306167ba5d8d48a62dbe5fd0d05e87c33c9784f08698f8a66b", "3b48a334dcf0a08bed2a9766fd553474ae3014db600b65573dfee0f183e9d1d9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("d317371cf2b4cd524849551ffd3b97d91edbc17f6b39c8693217383ba6a0370d", "9469268c421b7821f897deb2d4d2316b21ff5da35bef417aa4e284010ef78302", "3d8afae76c5982458849d21221e089ee161266a4248b12ea3048d1e79b76707e", "2ed6fdfa5f9120306167ba5d8d48a62dbe5fd0d05e87c33c9784f08698f8a66b", "3b48a334dcf0a08bed2a9766fd553474ae3014db600b65573dfee0f183e9d1d9") or SHA1 in~ ("d317371cf2b4cd524849551ffd3b97d91edbc17f6b39c8693217383ba6a0370d", "9469268c421b7821f897deb2d4d2316b21ff5da35bef417aa4e284010ef78302", "3d8afae76c5982458849d21221e089ee161266a4248b12ea3048d1e79b76707e", "2ed6fdfa5f9120306167ba5d8d48a62dbe5fd0d05e87c33c9784f08698f8a66b", "3b48a334dcf0a08bed2a9766fd553474ae3014db600b65573dfee0f183e9d1d9") or MD5 in~ ("d317371cf2b4cd524849551ffd3b97d91edbc17f6b39c8693217383ba6a0370d", "9469268c421b7821f897deb2d4d2316b21ff5da35bef417aa4e284010ef78302", "3d8afae76c5982458849d21221e089ee161266a4248b12ea3048d1e79b76707e", "2ed6fdfa5f9120306167ba5d8d48a62dbe5fd0d05e87c33c9784f08698f8a66b", "3b48a334dcf0a08bed2a9766fd553474ae3014db600b65573dfee0f183e9d1d9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["d317371cf2b4cd524849551ffd3b97d91edbc17f6b39c8693217383ba6a0370d", "9469268c421b7821f897deb2d4d2316b21ff5da35bef417aa4e284010ef78302", "3d8afae76c5982458849d21221e089ee161266a4248b12ea3048d1e79b76707e", "2ed6fdfa5f9120306167ba5d8d48a62dbe5fd0d05e87c33c9784f08698f8a66b", "3b48a334dcf0a08bed2a9766fd553474ae3014db600b65573dfee0f183e9d1d9"]);

                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or SHA1 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or MD5 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or SHA1 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or MD5 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

2026-06-17 9 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Tuesday added a maximum-severity security flaw impacting Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor (JCE) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-48907 (CVSS score: 10.0), is a case of improper access control that could facilitate arbitrary

Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] PHP webshell file actions originating from web server process (Beloved PBN wp_posts shell) · [LLM] WordPress backdoor admin account created via injected JavaScript (OptinMonster/TrustPulse supply chain)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Web-server process beacon to JCE/Beloved-PBN campaign IOC tidio.cc or 84.201.6.54 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Joomla JCE editor profile creation and PHP upload via unauthenticated endpoint (CVE-2026-48907) AIExploitation High
Hunts the article's specific JCE Editor exploit chain: unauthenticated POSTs to the JCE plugin endpoints (com_jce / jce / imgmanager) that create editor profiles and then upload .php / .phtml / .phar files. Targets web-tier telemetry where the exploit is observable. Rationale: Anchors directly on the JCE endpoints (com_jce / imgmanager / editor profile) named by CISA + Widget Factory's advisory, paired with PHP upload extensions. Cross-checked against the CISA KEV entry and Widget Factory 2.9.99.5 release notes. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://www.joomlacontenteditor.net/
ATT&CKT1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Joomla site admin updating JCE editor profiles from the back end
  • Webmaster uploading vetted PHP through the JCE file browser
  • Joomla penetration test exercising com_jce
  • Migration/backup tools writing PHP files into media/jce/
  • Authenticated content editor with profile-edit rights
Suppression filter
| where not (cIP in ("<admin-jumpbox-ip>")) and not (csUserAgent has "Joomla-Manage")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Confirm the source IP is not on the admin allowlist, pull the full request body / referer, and check whether the JCE component version is < 2.9.99.5 on the targeted host. Step 2 — Contain: Block the source IP at the WAF, quarantine and hash any PHP file dropped under /images, /components/com_jce, or /media/jce, and force a Joomla session reset. Step 3 — Hunt: Pivot on the offending source IP for other unauthenticated POSTs to com_jce across the estate, search wp/Joomla file systems for additional PHP shells matching the same SHA256, and review web server child processes spawned from w3wp/httpd/php-fpm in the last 7 days.
let JceEndpoints = dynamic(["com_jce","task=plugin","plugin=imgmanager","profile=Default"]);
let UploadExt = dynamic([".php",".phtml",".phar",".php5",".php7",".pht"]);
// Web shell file dropped under a Joomla content path by the web-server process
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm","nginx.exe","apache2")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\images\", @"\components\com_jce\", @"\media\jce\", @"\tmp\", @"/images/", @"/components/com_jce/", @"/media/jce/", @"/tmp/")
| where FileName has_any (UploadExt)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginIP
| order by Timestamp desc
let JceEndpoints = dynamic(["com_jce","task=plugin","plugin=imgmanager","profile=default","editor"]);
let UploadExt = dynamic([".php",".phtml",".phar",".php5",".pht"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod == "POST"
| where csUriStem has_any (JceEndpoints) or csUriQuery has_any (JceEndpoints)
| where scStatus < 400
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod == "POST"
| where RequestURL has_any (JceEndpoints)
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, DeviceAction),
(ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod == "POST"
| where Url has_any (JceEndpoints)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PHP webshell file actions originating from web server process (Beloved PBN wp_posts shell) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the Sucuri-described PHP web shell embedded in wp_posts that exposes read/write/edit/delete/chmod/upload over HTTP. Targets the web-server process (w3wp / php-fpm / httpd) performing untrusted file operations across the document root immediately after a POST hits /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php or /index.php. Rationale: Mirrors Sucuri's description of the wp_posts-resident shell that performs read/write/edit/delete/chmod/rename/upload over HTTP — only the web-server process should be writing PHP outside of plugin upgrade paths. Cross-referenced with the article's Sucuri callout. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sucuri.net/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate WordPress / Joomla plugin install or auto-update
  • Composer or wp-cli running PHP file deployments
  • Site-migration / staging-sync tooling (e.g. WP Migrate, Duplicator)
  • Cache plugins writing object-cache.php to wp-content/
  • Manual hotfix uploaded via SFTP that triggers web-server rewrite of .htaccess
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("wp-cli.phar","composer.phar","composer")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Pull every PHP/.htaccess write by the web-server process in the cluster, hash them and check whether they originate from an authentic plugin update by cross-checking against wp-admin/admin-ajax.php request logs. Step 2 — Contain: Take the host offline behind maintenance mode, snapshot disk + database (focus on wp_posts content where post_content begins with `<?php`), and rotate all wp-config secrets + DB creds. Step 3 — Hunt: Query for inbound HTTP requests with body parameters matching shell commands (read/write/edit/delete/chmod) over the last 30 days, search every site in the estate for wp_posts rows where post_content contains `<?php`, and review egress traffic from the web tier for the IOCs in UC4.
let WebServerProcs = dynamic(["w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm","nginx.exe","apache2"]);
let ShellExt = dynamic([".php",".phtml",".phar",".pht",".htaccess"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (WebServerProcs)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileDeleted")
| where FileName has_any (ShellExt) or PreviousFileName has_any (ShellExt)
| where FolderPath !has @"\wp-content\plugins\" and FolderPath !has @"\wp-content\upgrade\"
| summarize WriteCount = count(), DistinctPaths = dcount(FolderPath), SamplePath = any(FolderPath), SampleFile = any(FileName), arg_max(Timestamp, *)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where WriteCount >= 5 or DistinctPaths >= 3
| order by Timestamp desc
let WebServerProcs = dynamic(["w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm","nginx.exe","apache2"]);

WordPress backdoor admin account created via injected JavaScript (OptinMonster/TrustPulse supply chain) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the Sansec-described supply chain campaign where injected JS waits for a logged-in admin and silently submits POSTs to /wp-admin/user-new.php and /wp-admin/plugin-install.php to create a backdoor admin and install a self-hiding plugin. Pivots on unattended user/plugin creation calls coming from a logged-in admin session shortly after page load. Rationale: Anchored on the article's named WP admin endpoints (user-new.php / plugin-install.php) which the Sansec write-up identified as the actions the injected JS silently triggers in an admin session. Cross-checked against: • https://sansec.io/research/
ATT&CKT1136.001 T1505 T1195.002
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate site administrator manually creating a new editor / installing a plugin
  • Bulk WordPress provisioning via WP-CLI or a managed-hosting control panel
  • Pen-test exercise creating admin via the UI
  • Cookie-based plugin installer (e.g. ManageWP, Jetpack) actioning a fleet install
  • Authenticated admin walking through site-setup wizard
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Identify the WordPress site, confirm whether the source IP and User-Agent correspond to a known admin, and pull the list of users + plugins created in the last 7 days. Step 2 — Contain: Disable any user created in the suspicious window, remove unknown plugins, force password reset for all admins, rotate ABSPATH secrets/salts, and revoke active sessions. Step 3 — Hunt: Search the site's HTML for outbound JS includes pointing at OptinMonster/TrustPulse/PushEngage CDN paths that were compromised, audit wp_options for hidden-plugin flags (e.g. `active_plugins` containing entries that don't appear in wp-admin), and pivot on the source IP across all monitored sites.
let AdminCreateEndpoints = dynamic(["wp-admin/user-new.php","wp-admin/users.php","action=createuser","action=install-plugin","plugin-install.php"]);

(ImWebSession

Web-server process beacon to JCE/Beloved-PBN campaign IOC tidio.cc or 84.201.6.54 AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts outbound network connections or DNS queries to the article's named IOCs (tidio.cc, 84.201.6.54) — which the Beloved PBN Entegrasyonu fake plugin beacons to on every page load. Tier as alerting because both indicators are specific, low-volume, and second-source confirmed. Rationale: Both IOCs are named explicitly in the article (tidio.cc, 84.201.6.54). Specific enough to alert on outright; cross-checked against abuse.ch ThreatFox and the Sucuri write-up referenced in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://threatfox.abuse.ch/ • https://blog.sucuri.net/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate site using Tidio.com live-chat that mis-resolves to the typo-squat tidio.cc (rare but worth checking)
  • Threat-intel feed ingest tooling fetching the IOC for analysis
  • Security researcher pivot from a sandbox host
  • Mis-routed traffic on a shared NAT egress IP belonging to a hosting provider that legitimately uses 84.201.6.0/24
  • Scheduled IOC enrichment job pulling the domain into a TI platform
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("misp.exe","opencti.exe","powershell.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "ThreatIntel"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Confirm whether the source is a production web tier, identify the initiating process and parent, and check whether the site hosts WordPress or Joomla with the JCE plugin installed. Step 2 — Contain: Block 84.201.6.54 and *.tidio.cc at the perimeter (egress + DNS sinkhole), and isolate the affected web host pending PHP webshell hunt (see UC2). Step 3 — Hunt: Pivot on every host that resolved tidio.cc in the last 90 days, inspect wp_options / wp_posts for the Beloved PBN Entegrasyonu plugin signature, and search outbound page HTML for PBN backlinks injected into the footer.
let IocIPs = dynamic(["84.201.6.54"]);
let IocDomains = dynamic(["tidio.cc"]);
union

(DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
| where RemoteUrl has_any (IocDomains) or AdditionalFields has_any (IocDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, AdditionalFields)
| order by Timestamp desc
let IocIPs = dynamic(["84.201.6.54"]);
let IocDomains = dynamic(["tidio.cc"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationIP in (IocIPs) or DestinationHostName has_any (IocDomains) or RequestURL has_any (IocDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceAction),
(DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Name has_any (IocDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode),
(ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has_any (IocDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, EventResult),
(ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in (IocIPs) or DstHostname has_any (IocDomains) or Url has_any (IocDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol),
(W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where csReferer has_any (IocDomains) or csHost has_any (IocDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csUriStem, csHost, csReferer)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"

      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48907")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48907")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

[GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-49980: Rclone: Unauthenticated command execution in `rclone rcd --rc-serve` via inline remote instantiation, bypassing CVE-2026-41179 fix

GitHub Security Advisories
2026-06-16 6 use cases 1 technique 3 kill-chain phases detected

Rclone: Unauthenticated command execution in `rclone rcd --rc-serve` via inline remote instantiation, bypassing CVE-2026-41179 fix

CVEsCVE-2026-49980 CVE-2026-41179
ATT&CKT1190
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix
Phase 1
Reconnaissance
Detected
Phase 2
Weaponization
—
Phase 3
Delivery
Detected
Phase 4
Exploitation
Detected
Phase 5
Installation
Likely
Phase 6
Command & Control
Likely
Phase 7
Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Vulnerable rclone --rc-serve deployment without HTTP authentication · [LLM] Rclone RC listener bound to non-loopback interface via --rc-addr · [LLM] Devices with vulnerable rclone (CVE-2026-49980) in software inventory · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Browser process initiating connection to local rclone RC port 5572
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Rclone process spawns command interpreter (CVE-2026-49980 post-exploit)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Rclone process spawns command interpreter (CVE-2026-49980 post-exploit) AIExploitation High
Detects rclone spawning a shell or scripting interpreter, which is the observable behaviour when CVE-2026-49980 inline-remote backend options execute commands as the rclone process user. Rclone is a pure Go binary and does not normally shell out, so a process-tree pivot from rclone to bash/cmd/powershell/python is very high-fidelity evidence the unauthenticated RCE has fired. Rationale: Article confirms 'execute commands as the rclone process user' via inline backend option overrides. Rclone is a single-binary Go program with no legitimate need to fork shells/interpreters in production, so parent=rclone + child=shell is the cleanest post-exploit telemetry. Cross-checked against CCB Belgium advisory and rclone changelog confirming CVE-2026-49980 fixed in 1.74.3. Cross-checked against: • https://ccb.belgium.be/advisories/warning-two-critical-unauthenticated-code-execution-vulnerabilities-rclone-patch • https://securityonline.info/rclone-command-execution/ • https://rclone.org/changelog/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059 T1203
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Backup/DevOps wrapper scripts that invoke rclone from a shell and the shell parent is mis-attributed by Sysmon when rapid re-parenting happens
  • Rclone container images using shell-based ENTRYPOINT/CMD wrappers (entrypoint.sh) that re-exec rclone — child may appear inverted
  • Custom rclone backends using --script-pre-list or operator wrappers that legitimately fork helper interpreters
  • Admin live-troubleshooting rclone interactively from a shell pipe (rclone | jq, rclone | grep)
  • Container init systems (tini, dumb-init) that briefly mediate the rclone process tree
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/entrypoint.sh", "tini --", "dumb-init")) and not (ChildCmd has_any (" | jq", " | grep", " | awk", " | tee"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full child ProcessCommandLine and parent rclone command line; confirm parent rclone had --rc-serve and no --rc-user/--rc-pass/--rc-htpasswd flag. Check rclone version on host — vulnerable range is 1.55.0 to 1.74.2. 2) Contain: kill the rclone PID and any descendant processes; block inbound to the RC port (default 5572) at host firewall; if internet-facing, take the host off the network. Preserve memory if forensics is needed before kill. 3) Hunt: pivot on the host for any DeviceProcessEvents with rclone as ancestor in last 30 days, web-server / proxy logs for inbound GET/HEAD to port 5572, and outbound connections from the spawned shell (egress = data exfil or second-stage download). Check DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities for other hosts with the same CVE.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("rclone.exe", "rclone")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("rcd", "--rc-serve", "--rc ", "--rc-addr")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","bash","sh","dash","zsh","ksh","python","python3","perl","ruby","node")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentFolderPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildFolderPath = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ParentLeaf = tolower(tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "\\")[-1])),
         ChildLeaf  = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where ParentLeaf in ("rclone.exe", "rclone")
| where ChildLeaf in ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","bash","sh","dash","zsh","ksh","python","python3","perl","ruby","node")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Rclone Spawns Command Interpreter (CVE-2026-49980 RCE)
id: 9d2c3b1a-7e64-4c92-bd1f-d83f4a51e2c7
description: Detects rclone spawning a shell or scripting interpreter, indicating successful exploitation of CVE-2026-49980 unauthenticated command execution via the rclone rcd --rc-serve inline-remote attack.

logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\rclone.exe'
      - '/rclone'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'

      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/ksh'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'

Vulnerable rclone --rc-serve deployment without HTTP authentication AIReconnaissance High
Hunts for rclone processes started with the --rc-serve flag but without --rc-user, --rc-pass, or --rc-htpasswd — the exact precondition the advisory calls out as enabling unauthenticated CVE-2026-49980 RCE. Surfaces vulnerable surfaces before they are exploited. Rationale: Article explicitly states the preconditions: '--rc-serve flag must be in use' AND 'deployed without global RC HTTP authentication - so not using --rc-user/--rc-pass/--rc-htpasswd'. Detecting this combination on the command line directly enumerates the vulnerable population before an attacker reaches them. Validated against rclone docs and CCB Belgium advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://ccb.belgium.be/advisories/warning-two-critical-unauthenticated-code-execution-vulnerabilities-rclone-patch • https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_rcd/
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal-only lab rclone instances where auth is intentionally skipped because the host is air-gapped — still a misconfig but not exploitable
  • Rclone WebGUI demos / training environments
  • Rclone running with auth provided via env var or config file rather than CLI flag (real auth, false positive on this rule)
  • rclone rcd test runs by admins during config validation
  • Docker containers where rclone reads --rc-user from a mounted secret file using `--rc-user-from-file` style indirection
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the rclone version on the host (vulnerable range 1.55.0–1.74.2); check whether the host is reachable from untrusted networks (`netstat -ano | findstr 5572` or `ss -ltnp | grep 5572` and correlate to allowed-ingress firewall rules). 2) Contain: if internet-facing, add inbound block for TCP 5572 immediately; otherwise notify owner with 24h SLA to either upgrade to 1.74.3+, add --rc-user/--rc-pass, or stop using --rc-serve. 3) Hunt: pivot to last 30 days of inbound connections to port 5572 on that host and any rclone child-process shell-spawn events (UC1) to determine if exploitation has already occurred.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("rclone.exe", "rclone")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--rc-serve"
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--rc-user", "--rc-pass", "--rc-htpasswd"))
| extend RcAddr = extract(@"--rc-addr[\s=]+(\S+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, RcAddr, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend Leaf = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where Leaf in ("rclone.exe", "rclone")
| where CommandLine has "--rc-serve"
| where not (CommandLine has_any ("--rc-user", "--rc-pass", "--rc-htpasswd"))
| extend RcAddr = extract(@"--rc-addr[\s=]+(\S+)", 1, CommandLine)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, RcAddr
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Rclone RC listener bound to non-loopback interface via --rc-addr AIReconnaissance High
Hunts rclone processes started with --rc-addr pointing at a non-loopback address (any 0.0.0.0 / public IP / bare :port). The article notes 'by default rclone only serves the rc to localhost unless the --rc-addr flag is in use' — combined with the no-auth precondition this is the internet-exposed CVE-2026-49980 surface. Rationale: Article: 'by default rclone only serves the rc to localhost unless the --rc-addr flag is in use'. Detecting --rc-addr with a non-loopback value directly identifies the hosts whose RC API is reachable beyond the local box. The NoAuth flag in the projection lets analysts triage exposed+no-auth combos first. Validated against rclone --rc-addr docs. Cross-checked against: • https://rclone.org/rc/ • https://ccb.belgium.be/advisories/warning-two-critical-unauthenticated-code-execution-vulnerabilities-rclone-patch
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal rclone management cluster bound to a private RFC1918 admin VLAN (intentional, but should still be auth-protected)
  • Kubernetes deployments using 0.0.0.0:5572 because the pod has its own network namespace and access is mediated by NetworkPolicy/Service
  • rclone behind a reverse proxy that enforces auth at the proxy layer rather than rclone itself (RcAddr will look exposed but real exposure is mediated)
  • Developer host using --rc-addr=192.168.x.x for cross-VM testing
  • Cloud instances where security groups restrict 5572 even though rclone binds 0.0.0.0
Response runbook
1) Triage: resolve the bound interface — `netstat -ano | findstr 5572` / `ss -ltnp | grep 5572` — and check upstream firewall/security-group rules; pull host's external reachability test result. Confirm rclone version. 2) Contain: if internet-facing AND no --rc-user/--rc-pass, treat as compromise candidate — block port at edge, isolate host, run UC1 query backwards 30 days to check for prior shell-spawn evidence. If internal-only, file Sev3 to owner to add auth or rebind to localhost. 3) Hunt: enumerate all inbound source IPs to that host:port in last 30 days from firewall/flow logs; any non-corporate source is investigation-worthy.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("rclone.exe", "rclone")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--rc-addr"
| extend RcAddr = extract(@"--rc-addr[\s=]+(\S+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| where isnotempty(RcAddr)
| where not (RcAddr matches regex @"(?i)^(127\.0\.0\.1|localhost|\[?::1\]?)(:\d+)?$")
| extend NoAuth = not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--rc-user", "--rc-pass", "--rc-htpasswd"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, RcAddr, NoAuth
| order by NoAuth desc, Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend Leaf = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where Leaf in ("rclone.exe", "rclone")
| where CommandLine has "--rc-addr"
| extend RcAddr = extract(@"--rc-addr[\s=]+(\S+)", 1, CommandLine)
| where isnotempty(RcAddr)
| where not (RcAddr matches regex @"(?i)^(127\.0\.0\.1|localhost|\[?::1\]?)(:\d+)?$")
| extend NoAuth = not (CommandLine has_any ("--rc-user", "--rc-pass", "--rc-htpasswd"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, RcAddr, NoAuth
| order by NoAuth desc, TimeGenerated desc

Browser process initiating connection to local rclone RC port 5572 AIDelivery Medium
Detects a web browser opening a connection to 127.0.0.1:5572, which is the exact attack shape the advisory calls out: 'Firefox triggered the payload from a public HTTPS page containing only an <img> tag pointing at http://127.0.0.1:5572/...'. Browsers should never initiate traffic to the rclone RC port — any such hit is either an exploit attempt or a developer self-testing. Rationale: Article explicitly cites the browser-subresource attack: 'Firefox triggered the payload from a public HTTPS page containing only an <img> tag pointing at http://127.0.0.1:5572/...'. Browsers never legitimately talk to the rclone RC port, so any browser → 127.0.0.1:5572 hit is high-signal. Note: loopback capture must be enabled in the EDR/Sysmon config — vendor default for Defender is to capture it, Sysmon needs IncludeAll or an explicit rule. Cross-checked against: • https://rclone.org/rc/ • https://ccb.belgium.be/advisories/warning-two-critical-unauthenticated-code-execution-vulnerabilities-rclone-patch
ATT&CKT1189 T1190
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer using browser-based rclone Web GUI (rclone rcd --rc-web-gui) — legitimate but should still be reviewed for auth posture
  • Local devtools / Postman-like extensions running inside a Chromium-based app that happen to hit 5572 for testing
  • Rclone WebUI react app shipped via http://127.0.0.1:5572/ during admin operations
  • Browser-based monitoring dashboards that scrape rclone /core/stats
  • Security researcher / red team validating the CVE on a lab host
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--rc-web-gui", "rclone-webui-react")) and not (RemoteUrl has_any ("/rc-web-gui/", "/static/"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the Referer / RemoteUrl from the browser network event if available; check what tab/page the user was on (browser history, EDR's browser-events table). If the referer is an external site, it's drive-by attack. Pull any rclone child-process events on the same host within ±60s (cross-ref UC1). 2) Contain: if exploit chain confirmed, isolate host; force-quit rclone; block the referring external domain at proxy and notify user. If it's the rclone Web GUI, document and exclude that specific user/host combo. 3) Hunt: search proxy / DNS / UrlClickEvents for the referer domain across the fleet — same drive-by page may be targeting multiple rclone-on-localhost users; pivot to find other hosts with rclone listening on 5572 (UC2/UC3 results).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("firefox.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","chromium.exe","firefox","chrome","chromium","brave","opera")
| where RemoteIP in ("127.0.0.1","::1") and RemotePort == 5572
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
Event
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Source == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" and EventID == 3
| extend DestIp   = extract(@"DestinationIp:\s*([^\r\n]+)", 1, RenderedDescription),
         DestPort = extract(@"DestinationPort:\s*(\d+)", 1, RenderedDescription),
         Image    = tolower(extract(@"Image:\s*([^\r\n]+)", 1, RenderedDescription))
| where DestPort == "5572"
| where DestIp in ("127.0.0.1","::1")
| where Image has_any ("firefox.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","chromium.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Image, DestIp, DestPort
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Devices with vulnerable rclone (CVE-2026-49980) in software inventory AIReconnaissance High
Surfaces every device whose installed rclone version falls in the CVE-2026-49980 vulnerable range (1.55.0–1.74.2 for RCE; 1.46.0–1.74.2 for the file-read variant) using Defender TVM data. Patch-management pivot to drive remediation to 1.74.3+. Rationale: Article gives precise version range: 'Versions from 1.55.0 onwards are vulnerable to command execution. Earlier versions (from 1.46.0) are vulnerable to the unauthenticated local file read' and fixed package range 'vuln >= 1.46.0, <= 1.74.2'. Driving TVM directly off CveId is the cleanest patch-management pivot; the inventory-based fallback catches devices where the MDE catalog hasn't yet ingested the CVE. IsInternetFacing join surfaces the most urgent remediation targets. Cross-checked against: • https://rclone.org/changelog/ • https://www.cvedetails.com/product/48145/Rclone-Rclone.html • https://ccb.belgium.be/advisories/warning-two-critical-unauthenticated-code-execution-vulnerabilities-rclone-patch
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • MDE catalog lag — newly published CVE not yet enumerated for all devices (fallback inventory branch covers this)
  • Rclone embedded inside container images that MDE inventories at the host level (host showing vulnerable but actual usage is sandboxed)
  • Portable rclone.exe in user Downloads that's never executed
  • Vendor-bundled rclone shipped inside a third-party product (NAS sync utility) where the bundling vendor patches on its own cycle
  • Dev/test hosts intentionally pinned to a vulnerable version for regression testing
Response runbook
1) Triage: filter on IsInternetFacing=true first — those are the live exposures. For each host, confirm whether rclone is actually running with --rc-serve (cross-ref UC2 results) — vulnerable version + no RC server running = lower urgency. 2) Contain: queue upgrade to rclone 1.74.3+ via standard patch pipeline; for internet-facing hosts pending patch, add edge block on TCP 5572 as compensating control. 3) Hunt: for every vulnerable host, also look back 30 days for UC1 evidence (rclone spawning shell) and UC4 evidence (browser → localhost:5572). Any historical hit means assume-breach, escalate to IR.
let VulnByCve = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where CveId == "CVE-2026-49980"
    | project DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate;
let VulnByInventory = DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
    | where SoftwareName has "rclone"
    | extend Major = toint(extract(@"^(\d+)\.", 1, SoftwareVersion)),
             Minor = toint(extract(@"^\d+\.(\d+)", 1, SoftwareVersion)),
             Patch = toint(extract(@"^\d+\.\d+\.(\d+)", 1, SoftwareVersion))
    | where Major == 1 and (Minor < 74 or (Minor == 74 and Patch <= 2))
    | where Major == 1 and (Minor > 46 or (Minor == 46 and Patch >= 0))
    | project DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel = "Critical", RecommendedSecurityUpdate = "Upgrade to rclone 1.74.3+";
union VulnByCve, VulnByInventory
| summarize arg_max(SoftwareVersion, *) by DeviceId
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP) by DeviceId
  ) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-49980"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP) by DeviceId
  ) on DeviceName
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc

Vulnerable LiteLLM proxy (< 1.84.0) installed — CVE-2026-49468 exposure AIWeaponization High
Surfaces hosts running a LiteLLM Python package below 1.84.0, the version that patches the host-header auth bypass in litellm/proxy/auth/auth_utils.py::get_request_route(). Inventory-level early warning so the proxy can be upgraded before a request-layer detection ever has to fire. Rationale: Article names the exact patched version (1.84.0) and the vulnerable file path, so a TVM/inventory pivot on pip:litellm < 1.84.0 is the highest-confidence early-warning signal. Cross-checked GHSA-4xpc-pv4p-pm3w which confirms vuln range < 1.84.0 and the related BadHost / CVE-2026-48710 Starlette chain reported as actively exploited. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/releases/tag/v1.84.0 • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/litellm-flaw-cve-2026-42271-exploited.html • https://badhost.org/
ATT&CKT1190

  • Dev / staging boxes intentionally kept on an old LiteLLM version pinned for a model-routing regression test
  • Containers built from a frozen base image where the actual proxy is fronted by Cloudflare/WAF and not exposed
  • Air-gapped lab installs that match the version pattern but have no inbound 4000/8000 listener
  • Linux servers where TVM reports stale because the agent hasn't reported in ≥7 days

| where IsInternetFacing == true or PublicIP != ""
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the package version with `pip show litellm` on the host and check whether the proxy listener (4000/8000) is reachable from outside or only behind an LB/WAF that normalises Host. 2) Contain: if internet-exposed and no Host-validating front door is in place, restrict source IPs at the SG/firewall or front the listener with a `server_name` allowlist immediately; schedule the upgrade to ≥1.84.0 in the next change window. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC5/UC6 queries against this host's public IP for the last 30 days to see whether the bypass has already been exercised.
